## Introduction

This report compares the runtime of IF2 and the particle filter (`pfilter`) in
`pypomp` (GPU, and CPU where run) and R `pomp` (CPU) on identical work. For
panel measles, R uses `panelPomp`, and parameter estimation uses marginalized
panel iterated filtering (MPIF) in place of IF2.

| Model | Workload |
|---|---|
| SPX | The stochastic volatility model of @sun2024. Draws few random variates and takes a single `rproc` step per observation. |
| Dhaka cholera | A lightweight state transition run for 20 Euler steps per observation. Both implementations start from the same parameter vectors (`tests/dacca/starting_parameters.csv`). |
| Measles | London: 365 Euler steps per year across 14 years of weekly data, drawing 8 random variates per step (1 Poisson, 1 gamma, 6 binomial). Also compares the fast samplers in `pypomp.random` with stock `jax.random` samplers on the GPU. |
| Panel measles | London, Halesworth, Hastings and Cardiff, with shared and unit-specific parameters. |

Speedup and throughput use the cold-start particle filter (`pfilter_cold`),
which includes JIT compilation, since that cost is paid in practice. Throughput
is relative to a single R CPU core ($\text{speedup} \times N_{\text{cores}}$).

```{python Load results}
MODELS = ru.models("timing")
runs = {m: ru.load_runs(m, "timing") for m in MODELS}
tables = {
    m: ru.build_timing_comparison_df(runs[m], is_panel=ru.MODELS[m]["panel"]) for m in MODELS
}
```

## Visual review

- [Throughput](#throughput) and [results by model](#results-by-model):
  - SPX: `pypomp`'s throughput on GPU should be hundreds of times that of R
    `pomp` on one core, and `pypomp` on CPU should run at least twice as fast as
    R `pomp` on CPU.
  - Dhaka cholera: `pypomp`'s throughput on GPU should be thousands of times
    that of R `pomp` on one core, and the total speedup of `pypomp` on CPU
    relative to R `pomp` should be about 4x.
  - Measles: `pypomp`'s throughput on GPU with the fast samplers should be
    thousands of times that of R `pomp` on one core, and the fast-sampler GPU
    run should be substantially faster than the stock JAX sampler GPU run. We
    set no expectation for the CPU run.
  - Panel measles: `pypomp`'s throughput on GPU should be thousands of times
    that of R `panelPomp` on one core.

## Throughput

```{python Throughput plot}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5
CONFIG = {
    "R": "R",
    "gpu": "pypomp (GPU)",
    "gpu_jax": "pypomp (GPU, JAX samplers)",
    "cpu": "pypomp (CPU, 36 cores)",
}
frames = []
for m, df in tables.items():
    arms = ru.MODELS[m]["timing"]["arms"]
    frames.append(
        pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "Model": ru.MODELS[m]["label"],
                "Configuration": df["Configuration"].map(lambda c: CONFIG[arms[c]]),
                "throughput": pd.to_numeric(
                    df["Throughput (vs 1 R CPU core)"].str.rstrip("x"), errors="coerce"
                ),
            }
        )
    )
tp = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True).dropna()
tp["Model"] = pd.Categorical(tp["Model"], categories=tp["Model"].unique()[::-1])
tp["Configuration"] = pd.Categorical(tp["Configuration"], categories=list(CONFIG.values()))

(
    ggplot(tp, aes(x="Model", y="throughput", color="Configuration"))
    + geom_point(size=4, position=position_dodge(width=0.5))
    + scale_y_log10()
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(
        title="Throughput relative to one R CPU core",
        subtitle="Cold-start particle filter; log scale",
        x="",
        y="Throughput (× one R core)",
        color="Configuration",
    )
    + guides(color=guide_legend(nrow=2))
    + ru.scale_color_premium()
    + ru.theme_premium
)
```

## Results by model

The first `pfilter` call in JAX includes one-time JIT compilation. Later calls
run without recompiling, as the compilation overhead tables show.

```{python Results by model}
#| output: asis
for m in MODELS:
    print(ru.heading(m))
    print(ru.raw_html(tables[m].to_html(classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False)))
    print("\n**JIT compilation overhead**\n")
    cold_warm = ru.build_cold_vs_warm_df(runs[m])
    print(ru.raw_html(cold_warm.to_html(classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False)))
```
